3.4 Τοῦ αὐτοῦ· ἀναληπτικὰ δυνάμεωσ Μυρίς ἐστι βοτάνη τῷ κωνείῳ τὰ
πάντα παραπλησία πλὴν τοῦ ἄνθους, ὃ δὴ καὶ αὐτὸ ὅμοιον μέν ἐστι, μικρότερον δὲ
πολλῷ. Ῥίζαν δὲ ἔχει ὡς παρεμφέρουσαν ἐπιμήκη, εὐώδη σφόδρα καὶ ἡδίστην ἐν τῷ
τρώγειν. Εὑρίσκεται δὲ ἐν τοῖς ἐργασίμοις χωρίοις. Ταύτην ὁλόκληρον ἐπιμελῶς
τρίψας εἰς καθαρὰν πτισάνην εὖ μάλα ἑψημένην ἐμβάλλειν χρὴ καὶ συνεψεῖν
ἐπιμελῶς κινοῦντας. Ἔπειτα οἴνου εὐωδεστάτου τοσοῦτον ἐπιβάλλειν, ὡς μὴ λίαν
ἐξυγρᾶναι τὴν πτισάνην, καὶ νῆστιν ἐγχυματίζειν. Τούτου ἄμεινον βοήθημα πρὸς
τοῦτο οὐκ ἄν τις εὕροι· εἰ δὲ ἀπορεῖ τῆς ῥίζης, πτισάνῃ συνεψήσας ὑείους μυελοὺς
καὶ μάλιστα νωτιαίους οἴνῳ τε ὁμοίως ἐπιβαλών, δευτερεῦον ἕξει βοήθημα πρὸς τὸ
προκείμενον.
pass_a_gloss: 3.4 Of-the-same: restoratives of-strength. Myris is a-plant to-the hemlock the all-things similar except of-the flower, which indeed also itself similar on-the-one-hand is, smaller but by-much. A-root but it-has as somewhat-resembling elongated, fragrant very and most-pleasant in the eating. It-is-found but in the tillable fields. This whole carefully having-pounded into clean barley-gruel well indeed having-been-boiled to-put-in it-is-necessary and to-boil-together carefully stirring. Then of-wine most-fragrant so-much to-put-on, as not too-much to-make-wet the barley-gruel, and a-fasting-one to-drench. Than-this a-better help toward this not would anyone find; if but he-lacks of-the root, with-barley-gruel having-boiled-together swine marrows and especially spinal and with-wine similarly having-put-on, a-second-best he-will-have help toward the matter-at-hand.
pass_b_english: Of the same: restoratives of strength. Myris is a plant similar in all respects to hemlock except the flower, which is itself similar too, but much smaller. It has an elongated root, somewhat resembling, very fragrant and most pleasant to eat. It is found in cultivated fields.

Having pounded this whole plant carefully, one must put it into clean barley-gruel that has been well boiled, and boil them together carefully, stirring. Then add so much of the most fragrant wine as not to make the barley-gruel too liquid, and drench the one who is fasting. No one would find a better help than this for the purpose; but if he lacks the root, having boiled swine marrows — especially the spinal ones — together in barley-gruel and likewise added wine, he will have a second-best help for the matter at hand.

choices.why: Print plant-name similar to hemlock except the flower. Not σμύρνα (myrrh).

choices.english: similar in all respects to hemlock
choices.why: κώνειον is hemlock. Not a pine-cone.
Hippocratic ptisan, a boiled barley decoction. Not a paste.

choices.english: not to make the barley-gruel too liquid
choices.why: ἐξυγραίνω is to make too wet. The wine must not thin the gruel too far.
rejected: not to moisten only a little

choices.english: drench the one who is fasting
choices.why: νῆστιν is the accusative recipient. ἐγχυματίζω is the Cesti drench, not 'mix'.

choices.english: swine marrows, especially the spinal ones
choices.why: ὕειος is of swine; νωτιαῖος is the spinal marrow. Not generic marrow with a lacuna.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
